q: How do I know if AI trivia is accurate?
a: Spot-check the risky questions against one trusted source before the show — anything with a specific number, a precise date, a superlative like "first" or "largest," a recent event, or a named attribution. Broad, well-known facts almost never need checking; the errors hide in the specifics.

q: Which AI trivia questions are most likely to be wrong?
a: Questions with specific statistics, exact years, superlatives ("first," "only," "largest"), events from the last year or two, and "who invented/wrote/directed" attributions. A plausible-sounding wrong number looks identical to a right one, which is exactly why those need a second look.

q: Does the Trivia Show Maker fact-check questions for me?
a: It reduces the error rate — it generates at a low temperature, tells the model to skip anything it isn't confident about, and drops malformed multiple-choice questions — but it doesn't replace a quick human pass. Give your final set a five-minute spot-check of the risky questions before hosting.

q: How long does it take to fact-check a trivia set?
a: About five minutes, because you only need to verify the risky questions — the ones with numbers, dates, superlatives, or recent events — not all 40 or 50. Rewrite or cut anything you can't confirm in under a minute.
